close_reason: Done. BEGIN_BOUNDARY const moved to lib.rs:432, immediately after UTF8_BOM and before any use site.
description:
pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs:268 / 325 / 337 — `UTF8_BOM` is declared at line 268 (just before the `strip_bom` helper that uses it). `BEGIN_BOUNDARY` is first used at line 325 inside `from_pem` but is declared at line 337, AFTER the function that uses it. Rust accepts the forward reference at module scope, but the placement is awkward:

1. Reader scanning top-down hits the use at line 325, has to scroll past the function body to find the declaration at 337.
2. The two constants are conceptually related (both are PEM-parsing byte-literal sentinels) but are not co-located.

Fix: move `BEGIN_BOUNDARY` next to `UTF8_BOM` (line 269 or so), or group both in a single module-scope block before the first function that uses either. What goes wrong if it stays: minor code-organization debt; mildly harder to skim the module for 'what constants does this crate define'. Pure readability finding, no semantic effect.
title: BEGIN_BOUNDARY const declared 12 lines after first use, separated from related UTF8_BOM
